name: Long Call Calendar Spread
summary: Sell a near-term call and buy a longer-dated call at the same strike; bets the underlying pins near the strike while the front-month extrinsic decays faster than the back-month's.

legs.strike_rule: ATM by delta: |delta| 0.45-0.55 for a neutral calendar; 0.25-0.35 OTM call for a bullish directional calendar. Never pick a strike by intuition - pick it by delta, then confirm the strike is within 1.0 ATR(14) of spot.

legs.dte_rule: back leg, 45-70 DTE; gap between expiries 21-35 days

max_profit: No closed form. Approximately the theoretical value of the back-month call at front expiry with spot exactly at the strike, minus the net debit. Empirically 20-40% of the debit for a 30/60 ATM calendar. Model it with Black-Scholes using the back-month IV at T = (back DTE - front DTE)/365.
max_loss: The net debit paid, realized if the underlying finishes far enough from the strike in either direction that both legs carry near-identical (near-zero or near-parity) value at front expiry. Realized loss is capped only if the short leg is closed on time.
breakevens: Two, bracketing the strike; no closed form. Solve numerically at front expiry with the back-month IV. Rough rule for a 30/60 ATM calendar: strike +/- (1.0 to 1.3) x the debit converted to underlying points.

greeks.delta: ~0 at ATM (+/-0.05 per unit); grows to +/-0.15 as spot drifts off the strike
greeks.gamma: negative, ~-0.01 to -0.03 per unit; most negative at the strike into front expiry
greeks.theta: positive, ~+$3 to +$8/day per unit on a $100 underlying at 30/60
greeks.vega: positive (net long vega), ~+$8 to +$15 per unit; back-month vega exceeds front-month vega

when_to_use: IV rank of the underlying < 30 (you are net long vega, so buy back-month vol cheap - tastytrade prefers IVR under 10-20 for calendars). Term structure: want front IV - back IV >= 0 (flat to backwardated); reject if back IV exceeds front IV by more than 3 vol points, because you are then buying the expensive month and selling the cheap one. Best on range-bound, mean-reverting underlyings with a visible pin/magnet level (round numbers, high-OI strikes, prior VWAP consolidation).
entry_rules: Underlying IV rank < 30 AND IV percentile < 40.
front_IV - back_IV >= -3.0 vol points (reject steep contango).
Front leg DTE in [21,35]; back leg DTE in [45,70]; expiry gap in [21,35] days.
Strike selected by delta: neutral = front |delta| in [0.45,0.55]; directional = front |delta| in [0.25,0.35]. Strike must be within 1.0 x ATR(14) of spot.
Net debit per unit <= $2.50 on an underlying under $150, and total debit <= 2% of account equity ($1,000 on a $50k account).
Combined bid-ask of the two legs <= 10% of the net debit; reject if worse.
No earnings, no ex-dividend date, and no scheduled binary event between now and front expiry (unless running the earnings-calendar playbook explicitly).

LEVEL 3 OK: the long back-month call at the same strike, expiring later, fully covers the short front call. Submit as a single 2-leg mleg order. If Alpaca rejects the mixed-expiry mleg, leg in with the LONG back-month call filled FIRST, then sell the front - never the reverse.
Do not open if the front leg expires the same day (see zero-dte-day-calendar for that variant).
management_rules: Take profit at +25% of net debit (spread mark >= 1.25 x debit). 30-50% is acceptable on a wider-strike or longer-gap calendar; use 25% as the default machine target.
Stop out at -50% of net debit (spread mark <= 0.50 x debit).
Directional stop: close if |spot - strike| > 1.0 x the front-month ATM straddle price (the expected move) measured at entry.
Position delta cap: if |net delta| > 0.30 per unit, close or recenter to a new strike within 1 ATR of spot.

Roll the short leg out one expiry when front DTE <= 7 AND short |delta| <= 0.60 AND the short's remaining extrinsic <= 30% of its extrinsic at entry. Roll for a credit only; if the roll is a debit, close the whole structure.
Portfolio cap: max 4 concurrent calendar units per underlying; total capital in all calendars <= 10% of equity.
exit_rules: Close the entire spread no later than 2 trading days before front expiry unless the short leg is being rolled.
HARD RULE: close or roll the short call by 14:30 ET on its expiration day, unconditionally, regardless of P&L. American, share-settled options are never carried into expiration.
Close the short call immediately if its extrinsic value <= $0.05 per share OR short |delta| >= 0.90 (early-assignment window is open).
Close the short call before the close of the session preceding ex-dividend if the short call's extrinsic value < the declared dividend per share.
When unwinding leg-by-leg rather than as an mleg, BUY BACK THE SHORT LEG FIRST, then sell the long - never leave a naked short.
If the long back-month call marks below $0.10, close both legs; the structure is dead.
assignment_risk: Only the short front-month call is assignable. American style, settles in 100 shares. Trigger conditions: short call goes ITM and extrinsic collapses below ~$0.05, or the day before ex-dividend when extrinsic < dividend. If assigned, the account is short 100 shares against a long back-month call (a covered short at level 3): the system must buy the shares back within the same or next session and then decide whether to keep or sell the long call.
buying_power: Net debit only. Alpaca reserves the debit; no additional maintenance requirement while both legs are open. If the short is assigned, the short stock position creates a real margin requirement until flattened.
liquidity_needs: Both expirations: open interest >= 250 per leg, daily volume >= 50, quoted spread <= $0.10 on a leg priced around $2. Underlying ADV >= 2M shares. Reject any calendar whose back-month is quoted more than $0.25 wide - exit slippage destroys the edge.
common_mistakes: Opening calendars when IV rank is high (the net long vega gets crushed); ignoring that the back month's IV can drop even while spot pins perfectly; letting the short leg run to expiry; picking the strike where you hope price goes rather than where it is likely to pin; using an illiquid back month so that exit slippage exceeds the theoretical profit; forgetting the ex-dividend assignment window on dividend ETFs and dividend payers.
zero_dte_notes: A 0DTE front leg converts this into the day calendar (see zero-dte-day-calendar). On share-settled SPY/QQQ the 0DTE short leg carries pin and assignment risk, so only the dedicated day-calendar playbook with its forced 14:30 ET close should ever run it.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
